A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CHATS research. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original text-to-image benchmark evaluations, ablations, throughput measurements, and qualitative results in Section 5 and Appendices C–E.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and their results, including evaluations of SD1.5, SDXL, and In-house T2I.

M1.justification: The two-model architecture, training objectives, sampling distribution, and proxy-prompt approximation remain unchanged. The new theoretical material analyzes the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use Pick-a-Pic v2 and OpenImagePreferences for finetuning and the same HPS v2, GenEval, and DPG-Bench evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Standard models and Diffusion-DPO remain the comparators in corresponding benchmark tables. The comparator configurations in the ablation and dataset comparisons are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendix B retain the same models, sample counts, optimizers, batch size, resolution, learning rate, metrics, and sampling settings. No experimental protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: The component ablation, finetuning-dataset comparison, alpha sensitivity analyses, throughput comparison, and qualitative examples are retained without substantive changes.

E5.justification: Both versions report GenEval results averaged over four random seeds. Neither adds uncertainty intervals, significance tests, or other statistical reporting practices.

E6.justification: Tables 1–9 retain identical numerical entries. The sensitivity curves and qualitative image samples also match; displaced tables and figures contain retained results.

T1.justification: v1 provides reward-optimum and training-loss derivations in A.1–A.2. v2 adds A.3, claiming convergence under L-smoothness and equivalence to DPO's optimum, and A.4, deriving the existing sampler through Bayesian classifier signals and a new approximate-equality assumption for unconditional marginals. These substantially extend the theoretical scope.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same scientific contributions: combining preference alignment with sampling, using separate preference models, achieving data efficiency, and outperforming the reported baselines.

C2.justification: A.4 adds a mechanism explanation based on combined classifier-like signals, interpreting the dispreferred conditional-to-unconditional ratio as adjusting guidance. Existing empirical interpretations and the throughput limitation remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract now states that code is publicly available and supplies a repository address, absent from v1. Implementation and experimental details otherwise remain unchanged; repository contents were not accessed.

R1.justification: The bibliography and related-work discussion are retained, but A.3 newly asserts that CHATS recovers the same optimal joint distribution as traditional DPO, extending its claimed theoretical relationship to prior work.

P1.justification: v2 adds two appendix subsections and a corresponding cross-reference, a code-availability sentence, and an additional correspondence contact. The existing narrative and section organization are largely retained.

P2.justification: All nine tables and ten figures are retained. Their placement and surrounding spacing change, including relocating Table 3 and placing Figure 5 on a separate page; the abstract also extends onto page 2.

improvement.justification: The code-access information and A.4's explicit sampler rationale improve documentation. However, new A.3 asserts DPO-optimum equivalence without establishing it, and its convergence inequality lacks a stated step-size condition. Its affine-reward invariance claim also sits uneasily with the scale-dependent policy in Eq. 45. These useful clarifications and new rigor concerns leave the net quality effect uncertain; the empirical evidence is unchanged.
